tytul: Smoked sprats and herring: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for sprats and herring smoked at home, including whole, ungutted fish.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to the FDA, gut any fish before salting, drying, pickling or fermenting it.
The FDA considers uneviscerated (ungutted) fish that are salt-cured, dried or smoked a potentially life-threatening health hazard.

akapity: According to the FDA, small uneviscerated fish under 5 inches, such as anchovies and sprats, may be left ungutted only if the process eliminates any toxin already formed and stops toxin forming during processing, and the finished product has 10% salt in the water phase (refrigerated) or a water activity below 0.85 or a pH of 4.6 or below (shelf stable).
According to the FDA, such ungutted fish products are hazardous whether they are stored at room temperature, in the refrigerator or in the freezer.
The FDA may act against uneviscerated salt-cured, dried or smoked fish more than 5 inches long.
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for smoking ungutted sprats or herring from a checked source.
Wisconsin Sea Grant and University of Minnesota Extension have a method for hot smoking fish at home that has been scientifically tested for safety.
In that method, the fish are first gutted and gilled, the kidney is removed from the belly cavity, and all exposed surfaces are rinsed with fresh water.
The internal temperature of the fish must reach 160 °F and stay there for at least 30 minutes; if your smoker cannot do this, finish cooking the fish in the oven within 2 hours of smoking.
JarAtlas describes hot smoking of some gutted fish, such as mackerel, on separate cards.
